رَاشِنٌ i. q. طُفَيْلِىٌّ; (S, K;) i. e. One who comes to a feast uninvited thereto: he who watches for the time of food, and then goes in to the party when they are eating, is termed وَارِشٌ. (S.) ―
-b2- And One who eats all that is upon the table of food; syn. مِقَمٌّ: in the K, المُقِيمُ is erroneously put for المِقَمُّ. (TA.) ＝
-A2- Also A small gift to the pupil of the صَائِغ [or goldsmith]; in Pers, called شاكردانه [correctly شَاكِرْدَانَهْ]. (K. [ما يُرْضَحُ in the CK is a mistake for ما يُرْضَخُ.])
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
